_about: Input to scripts/build_journal.py (journal v2). renders = every image the site shows and the linear files its numbers are measured on. timeline = the honest dated sequence (each step's after is the best image I had on that date, made with that date's code; before = the previous step's after). stages = the one-change comparisons ('What each change did'), reprocessed 17 Oct. hero = first light vs the latest timeline step. Paths are relative to the repo root (data/ is never published).

frame._rule: Site standard (2026-10-17): M31 shown horizontal, as the Seestar's portrait frames capture it (no rotation), cropped to a 4:3 landscape window around the nucleus, moved up so M110 is in frame and M32 sits below the core. Same crop for both sides of a pair.

timeline.title: My first pipeline
timeline.what_changed: I copied the 7/8 Sep subs off the scope and ran my own first pipeline on them: frame QA, Siril drizzle stacking weighted towards the sharpest frames, and GraXpert's AI background removal.
timeline.what_it_did: Stars shrank from {before.fwhm_arcsec}″ to {after.fwhm_arcsec}″, but SNR at my eight test points in the disc fell from {before.snr_headline} to {after.snr_headline}. Culling and sharpness weighting threw signal away, and the AI background model took part of the halo with it.

timeline.title: After the review
timeline.what_changed: The next day I had the pipeline reviewed against this night's data and acted on what it measured: no trend-based frame culling, weighting by star count instead of sharpness, a plain plane fit for the background, and star removal with Dark Star, including a fix for the dark ring it left around the core.
timeline.what_it_did: With {after.frames} frames instead of {before.frames}, SNR went from {before.snr_headline} to {after.snr_headline} (+{d.snr_pct} %) and stars grew from {before.fwhm_arcsec}″ to {after.fwhm_arcsec}″. The stack is bit for bit what today's pipeline makes from this night.

timeline.title: A second night, under a full moon
timeline.provenance: saved run history, 16 Oct (commit 63e7708 + uncommitted changes)
timeline.what_changed: I added {r[s0925_529_asof][frames]} frames from 25/26 Sep, shot under a {n[2026-09-25][moon][illum_pct]:.0f} % moon while the rest were still on the scope, and stacked both nights frame by frame with noise weighting.
timeline.what_it_did: SNR rose from {before.snr_headline} to {after.snr_headline} and stars tightened from {before.fwhm_arcsec}″ to {after.fwhm_arcsec}″, from {after.minutes:.0f} minutes stacked.

side_notes.label: 25/26 Sep alone, 529 frames
side_notes.text: On its own the moonlit night reached SNR {note.snr_headline} from {note.minutes:.0f} minutes, with stars at {note.fwhm_arcsec}″.

timeline.title: Three nights
timeline.what_changed: I added 16/17 Oct and the rest of 25/26 Sep, then reprocessed all three nights with today's pipeline, which also changed the colour calibration.
timeline.what_it_did: {after.frames} frames and {after.minutes:.0f} minutes took SNR from {before.snr_headline} to {after.snr_headline} and stars from {before.fwhm_arcsec}″ to {after.fwhm_arcsec}″.

side_notes.label: 16/17 Oct alone
side_notes.text: My sharpest night: {note.fwhm_arcsec}″ stars and SNR {note.snr_headline} from {note.minutes:.0f} minutes, reprocessed 17 Oct.

side_notes.label: 25/26 Sep alone, all frames
side_notes.text: With every frame copied, the moonlit night alone kept {note.frames} frames and reached SNR {note.snr_headline}, stars {note.fwhm_arcsec}″.

stages.title: Measure, don't guess
stages.what_changed: Reprocessed today: the 7/8 Sep frames through my first pipeline and through today's, which keeps almost every frame, weights them by star count and fits the background with a flat plane instead of an AI model.
stages.what_it_did: On the same night SNR went from {before.snr_headline} to {after.snr_headline} (+{d.snr_pct} %), and stars grew from {before.fwhm_arcsec}″ to {after.fwhm_arcsec}″.

stages.title: The full moon night
stages.what_changed: Reprocessed today with the same pipeline: the dark 7/8 Sep night against all of 25/26 Sep, under a {n[2026-09-25][moon][illum_pct]:.0f} % moon.
stages.what_it_did: Moonlight raised the frame background to {n[2026-09-25][sky_adu]:.0f} ADU from {n[2026-09-07][sky_adu]:.0f}, so {after.minutes:.0f} minutes gave SNR {after.snr_headline} where {before.minutes:.0f} dark minutes gave {before.snr_headline}. Stars came out at {after.fwhm_arcsec}″ against {before.fwhm_arcsec}″.

stages.title: A ring around the core
stages.what_changed: Reprocessed today on all of 25/26 Sep: star removal with the old core protection, a fixed brightness threshold, against the new one, set relative to the nucleus.
stages.what_it_did: The old threshold left a dark ring {before[ring][radius_arcmin]}′ from the nucleus, where the brightness dipped {before[ring][depth_pct]} %. With the new one no dip is deeper than {after[ring][depth_pct]} %.

stages.title: Stacking nights
stages.what_changed: Reprocessed today: my best single night by SNR, 7/8 Sep, against all three nights stacked frame by frame with noise weighting.
stages.what_it_did: {after.frames} frames over {after.minutes:.0f} minutes lifted SNR from {before.snr_headline} to {after.snr_headline} (+{d.snr_pct} %). Minutes alone would predict +{d.sqrt_t_pct} %, but the moonlit frames are noisier.

stages.title: Fixing the lavender
stages.what_changed: Reprocessed today on the two-night stack: Siril's photometric calibration against the NOMAD catalogue, as I first ran it, against local Gaia with a correction to the spectrophotometric balance.
stages.what_it_did: The disc's blue-to-green ratio went from {before[color][b_over_g]} to {after[color][b_over_g]} and red-to-green from {before[color][r_over_g]} to {after[color][r_over_g]}, which takes out the lavender cast.
